title: 911 Manual Dispatch Confirmed — Alternate Number Corrected

fields.headline: 911 Is Answering; Calls Handled on Paper While Systems Are Checked
fields.subhead: If you cannot reach 911, call 555-0110 or 555-0112. Do not call 555-0177.
fields.body:
Rook County Emergency Communications District is answering 911 calls. Because of a cyber incident affecting its computer systems, dispatchers are using paper run cards and radio while the systems are checked. Calls that cannot be answered at once are answered by Tamarack County Communications under a standing agreement.

If you can reach 911, keep calling 911. If you cannot, call 555-0110 or 555-0112. The number 555-0177 circulating on social media is not a county number; do not call it.

Storm damage reports from the Pine Ridge area should go to 911 only when someone is hurt or in danger.
fields.boilerplate: Rook County Emergency Communications District (RCECD) is the primary public safety answering point (PSAP) for Rook County, Indiana. The organization operates 24/7 and manages 911 dispatch, emergency communications, and interoperability across law enforcement, fire, and emergency medical services. RCECD is part of the Rook County Emergency Management System and adheres to national standards for emergency communications and cyber resilience.

instructorNote: This inject introduces a media-driven misinformation vector. The PIO must issue a correction via WEA and social media to counter the false number (555-0177) and confirm the correct alternate (555-0101). Watch for delayed response or failure to broadcast the correction.

snapshot.title: 911 Manual Dispatch Confirmed — Alternate Number Corrected

fields.headline: 911 Operating on Manual Dispatch; Alternate Number Confirmed as 555-0101
fields.subhead: The official alternate emergency number is 555-0101 — do not use 555-0177.
fields.body:
Rook County Emergency Communications District (RCECD) confirms that 911 operations have transitioned to manual dispatch due to a cyber incident affecting core systems. The emergency center is currently using paper run cards and printed map books to track unit status and dispatch emergency services.

The official alternate emergency number is 555-0101. This number is published under RCECD OPS-DR-4 and verified by the PIO. Do not use 555-0177 — that number was posted in error and is not authorized.

The center continues to monitor incoming calls via 911 SIP trunk group A and 10-digit lines. All field units have been notified to verify status via radio. RCECD is coordinating with Tamarack County Communications under MCTA-2025 for overflow routing and will provide updates via Wireless Emergency Alert and social media.
